p0.original: 关键问题：什么过程控制了我们的情绪

p2.original: 大脑中有两种情绪处理系统：一种是有意识的，另一种是无意识的。这个发现为一些关于情绪与认知的早期争论提供了新的思路。
p2.en: There are two emotional systems in the brain: conscious and unconscious. This discovery has provided new ideas for some early debates about emotions and perceptions.

p3.original: 假设你在万圣节玩鬼屋探险，这时一个电影人物用幽灵般“嘘”的语气吓了你一跳！你立即就出现了情绪反应。它可能涉及一种外部反应，如跳起来、喘粗气或大声尖叫。与此同时，你也会对身体的化学变化做出反应，内部器官的功能发生变化，大脑和自主神经系统的某些部位受到刺激。此外，当你意识到你真的没有危险（只是被一个裹着床单的人吓到）时，内部的情绪反应（如加速的心跳）仍会持续很长一段时间。
p3.en: Suppose you're on a ghosthouse expedition on Halloween, and then a movie character scares you with ghost-like "shh" tone! You immediately had an emotional reaction. It may involve an external reaction, such as jumping up, breathing rough or screaming loudly. At the same time, you will react to chemical changes in the body, changes in the functioning of internal organs and stimulation of certain parts of the brain and the autonomous nervous system. Moreover, when you realize you're not really in danger (scared by a man with a sheet), internal emotional reactions (such as an accelerated heartbeat) continue for a long time.

p4.original: 这表明情绪在有意识和无意识的层面都会起作用，这让我们想到了心理学最近的一个伟大发现：大脑中存在两条情绪通路。这个双通路就是这一部分核心概念的焦点。
p4.en: This shows that emotions work at both the conscious and the unconscious levels, and it reminds us of a recent great discovery in psychology: two emotional pathways in the brain. This dual access is the focus of this core concept.

p5.original: 大脑中有两种情绪处理系统：一种是有意识的，另一种是无意识的，这个发现为一些关于情绪与认知的早期争论提供了新的思路。
p5.en: There are two types of emotional treatment systems in the brain: conscious and unconscious, which provide new ideas for some early debates about emotions and perceptions.

p6.original: 在接下来的内容中，我们将看到“年轻”的情绪神经科学会如何阐述情绪的产生机制。尽管细节还不是特别清楚，但我们已经大致了解了大脑中的情绪回路及其与全身的联系。所以在这部分的最后，我们将首先看到这两种情绪系统是如何工作的。然后我们将看到它们是如何帮助解决一些早期争论的。在这部分的最后，我们将转向一个实际应用，了解情绪唤醒会如何影响我们在考试或体育比赛中的成绩。
p6.en: In the next section, we will see how the “young” emotional neurosciences will describe the mechanisms for the creation of emotions. Although the details are not particularly clear yet, we have a general understanding of the emotional circuits in the brain and their connection to the whole body. So at the end of this segment, we will first see how these emotional systems work. Then we will see how they helped resolve some of the early debates. At the end of this segment, we will turn to a practical application to understand how emotional awakening can affect our performance in examinations or sports games.

p14.original: 描述大脑中的两种情绪系统及其功能。
p14.en: It describes two emotional systems in the brain and their functions.

p15.original: 对蛇或蜘蛛有强烈恐惧的人，他们通常明白自己的反应是不理智的，然而，他们似乎无法克制这种情绪。但是一个人怎么能同时拥有两种相互冲突的情绪呢？答案就在神经科学家约瑟夫·勒杜（Joseph LeDoux，1996，2000）发现的大脑的两种截然不同的情绪处理系统中。
p15.en: Those who are strongly afraid of snakes or spiders usually understand that their reaction is irrational, but they seem to be unable to contain it. But how can a person have two conflicting emotions at the same time? The answer lies in two very different emotional systems of the brain found by neuroscientist Joseph LeDoux, 1996.

p17.original: 第一种情绪处理系统——快速反应系统，主要是在无意识层面运行的。它能快速筛选传入的刺激，帮助我们在潜在危险事件发生前迅速做出反应。这个系统与内隐记忆有关，起到一种早期预警和防御的作用，例如，一个徒步旅行者看到蛇时，几乎瞬间就会产生恐惧反应（Helmuth，2003b）。它主要依赖于深层脑回路，尤其是边缘系统的自动运行，无须刻意进行意识控制（见图9-9）。
p17.en: The first emotional system — the rapid response system — operates mainly at the unconscious level. It can quickly screen inbound stimulus and help us react quickly before potential dangerous events occur. The system is related to hidden memory and serves as an early warning and defence, for example, when a traveller sees a snake, he reacts almost instantaneously to fear (Helmuth, 2003b). It relies mainly on deep brain circuits, especially the automatic operation of peripheral systems, without conscious control (see figures 9-9).

p18.original: 无意识的情绪对曾经在人类历史上构成威胁的某些刺激具有内在的敏感性。此外，这种快速反应系统可以很容易地通过经典条件反射习得新的恐惧。这就解释了为什么人们对蜘蛛和蛇的恐惧要比对电力和汽车等新事物的恐惧更为普遍。现在这些新事物造成的死亡人数远比蜘蛛和蛇多，但这些都只是最近才开始对我们的生存构成威胁的。
p18.en: Ignorant sentiments are inherently sensitive to certain incentives that once posed a threat in the history of humankind. In addition, such a rapid response system can easily resonate with new fears through classic conditions. This explains why fear of spiders and snakes is more common than fear of new things such as electricity and cars. These new things now cause far more deaths than spiders and snakes, but they have only recently begun to threaten our very existence.

p19.original: 你可以看到这种快速响应系统的配置是如何自适应的，宁愿过于谨慎也不要冒险犯错。不幸的是，快速反应系统也是一个“慢慢忘记”的系统，这使得焦虑和恐惧难以消除，有时甚至会发展成更严重的问题，即恐怖症。但对我们的祖先来说，这种缓慢的遗忘具有生存优势，可以使他们更容易记住危险的情况，如潜伏在水坑边的捕食者。
p19.en: You can see how this rapid response system is configured to fit itself, rather than risk making mistakes. Unfortunately, the rapid response system is also a “slow forget” system, which makes anxiety and fear difficult to overcome and, in some cases, even more serious problems, namely, the symptoms of terror. But for our ancestors, this slow oblivion has the advantage of survival, making it easier for them to remember dangerous situations, such as predators lying by the water pit.

p21.original: 第二种情绪系统——涉及意识处理的系统，其反应相对较慢。它的联系主要在大脑皮层，尤其包括外显记忆（LeDoux，1996；Mather，2007）。这种慢速反应系统使我们的徒步旅行者（见图9-9）在往往能让他联想到危险动物的地方变得谨慎。因为意识系统使用的脑回路与那些支持无意识情绪处理的脑回路不同，你对事件的认识会与你的无意识唤醒的情绪有很大的不同。因此，如果你有恐怖症，你可以真正持有“两个想法”：尽管“知道”这种恐惧感没有理智基础，但仍会感到恐惧。然而，这两个系统在“忘记恐惧记忆”的速度上都很慢。
p21.en: The second emotional system — a system involving conscious processing — is relatively slow in response. Its links are mainly in the cerebral cortex, including, in particular, outward memory (LeDoux, 1996); Mather, 2007. This slow-response system makes our hikers (see figures 9-9) more cautious where he is often associated with dangerous animals. Because the mind system uses a different brain circuit than those that support unconsciousness, your perception of events is quite different from your unconscious awakening. So, if you have a phobia, you can really hold the “two ideas”: even though “know” this fear has no basis in reason, it still feels fear. However, both systems are slow in “forget fear memory”.

p23.original: 特别值得一提的是，大脑左右两个额叶在控制情绪方面起着互补的作用。正如大脑皮层的不同部位会产生不同的感觉一样，积极和消极的情绪分别与大脑的两个半球有关，这种效应被称为情绪偏侧化。其证据来自正常人情绪反应的脑电图记录，以及右半球或左脑半球受损的人的脑电图（Davidson et al.，2000）。一般来说，右脑半球专门处理负面情绪，如愤怒和抑郁；而左脑半球则处理更积极的、愉快的情绪（Kosslyn et al.，2002）。
p23.en: Of particular note is the complementary role played by the brain and the two foreheads in emotional control. Just as different parts of the cortex of the brain have different feelings, positive and negative emotions are related to the two hemispheres of the brain, and this effect is called emotional slantification. Evidence is drawn from the electro-brain record of normal human emotional reactions, as well as from the electro-brain map of people who have suffered damage in the right or left hemispheres (Davisson et al., 2000). In general, the right hemisphere specializes in dealing with negative emotions, such as anger and depression; The left is dealing with more positive and pleasant emotions (Kosslyn et al., 2002).

p24.original: 图9-9 两种处理情绪的脑回路
p24.en: Figure 9-9: Two brain circuits to deal with emotions

p25.original: 注：快速（无意识）回路将视觉信息从丘脑直接传递到杏仁核，迅速激活恐惧和回避反应。慢速（有意识的）回路通过视觉皮层的路径更长，在到达杏仁核之前会对刺激做出更完整的评估。
p25.en: Note: Rapid (intentional) circuits transmit visual information directly from the hypothalamus to almond cores and quickly activate fear and avoid reaction. Slow (conscious) circuits take longer paths through the visual cortex, with a more complete assessment of the stimulation before reaching almond cores.

p26.original: 9.10.4 大脑皮层与边缘系统的连接
p26.en: 9.10.4 Relationship of the cerebral cortex to the peripheral system

p27.original: 现在的神经科学家认为，他们已知道了情绪和理性在大脑中的相遇之处，即有意识的情绪处理途径与边缘系统的连接。这是一小块有着响亮名字的脑区：腹内侧前额皮层（Ventromedial Prefrontal Cortex，VMPFC）。VMPFC位于大脑额叶的底部，就在眼睛后面，它与杏仁核和海马都有着广泛的联系（Barrett & Wager，2006；Wagar & Thagard，2006）。在那里，VMPFC将外部刺激和有意识的记忆与身体的“内脏”反应混合在一起，就像录音师将输入的信息组合成音轨一样。这是积极的还是消极的？你起鸡皮疙瘩了吗？你觉得喉咙哽咽了吗？你感觉胃里有个结吗？多亏了你的VMPFC，你的大部分记忆都可能跟内脏关联在一起。
p27.en: Now neuroscientists believe that they know what happens to emotions and reason in the brain, that is, the conscious emotional approach that connects to peripheral systems. It's a small brain area with a loud name: the inner frontal cortex (VMPFC). VMPFC, located at the bottom of the forehead of the brain, is behind its eyes and has extensive links to almond cores and seahorses (Barrett & Wager, 2006); Wagar & Thagard, 2006. There, VMPFC mixes external irritation and conscious memory with the body's “intestine” reaction, just as the recorder combines the input into a track. Is that positive or negative? Are you having a goose bump? Do you feel your throat strangling? Do you feel a knot in your stomach? Thanks to your VMPFC, most of your memories may be connected to the internal organs.

p28.original: VMPFC后面是伏隔核，这一脑区主要负责积极的感受。人们认为，当我们获得奖励时，伏隔核会给我们带来愉快的感觉。顺便一提，当我们听喜欢的音乐或看到喜欢的人时，该大脑区域就会变得异常活跃，并释放多巴胺（Gaidos，2010；Levitin，2006）。
p28.en: Behind the VMPFC is an impregnated nucleus, which is primarily responsible for positive feelings. It is believed that when we get the reward, the nucleus will give us a pleasant feeling. By the way, when we listen to the music we like or see the people we like, the brain area becomes extremely active and releases dopamine (Gaidos, 2010); Levitin, 2006.

p29.original: 如图9-10所示，这种快速而无意识的情绪回路也与大脑的边缘系统相连。位于脑干上方的那层边缘结构无疑进化成了掌控攻击、防御和撤退行为的控制系统，即控制“战斗或逃跑”反应（Caldwell，1995；LeDoux，1994，1996）。这方面的证据来自损伤（切除）或电刺激边缘系统的部分，它们可以造成人们在情绪反应方面的巨大变化。被驯服的动物可能成为杀手，而猎物和捕食者可能成为友好的同伴，这些都取决于边缘系统的哪个部分受到影响（Delgado，1969）。
p29.en: As shown in figures 9-10, this rapid and unconscious emotional circuit is also linked to the peripheral system of the brain. The edge structure above the brain stem has undoubtedly evolved into a control system to control attacks, defenses and evacuations, i.e. to control “combat or escape” reactions (Caldwell, 1995); LeDoux, 1994, 1996. Evidence in this regard comes from the part of the impairment (corruption) or electro-stimulatory peripheral systems that can cause dramatic changes in emotional responses. A tamed animal may be a killer, while prey and predators may be friendly companions, depending on which part of the peripheral system is affected (Delgado, 1969).

p30.original: 杏仁核在恐惧情绪中的重要性得到了很好的证明（LeDoux，1996；Whalen，1998；Winkielman et al.，2007）。就像看门狗一样，杏仁核会对危险保持警惕（Hamann et al.，2002；Helmuth，2003a）。正如你在图中所看到的，杏仁核接收的信息不仅来自快速且无意识的情绪处理回路，还来自反应时间又长又慢的意识回路。
p30.en: The importance of almonds in fear is well demonstrated (LeDoux, 1996); Whalen, 1998; Winkielman et al., 2007). Like a guard dog, almond cores are alert to danger (Hamann et al., 2002); Helmuth, 2003a. As you can see in the picture, almond cores receive information not only from rapid and unconscious emotional processing circuits, but also from long and slow response time.

p31.original: 图9-10 腹内侧前额皮层区和伏隔核
p31.en: Figure 9-10 Frontal cortex area and voltary nucleus on the inner side

p32.original: 注：腹内侧前额皮质区和伏隔核都位于大脑的中线，位于两个脑半球之间。
p32.en: Note: Both the front cortex area and the voltary nucleus on the inside of the abdomen are located in the middle of the brain and between the two hemispheres.

p34.original: 在早期，人们寻找过控制特定情绪的大脑“中心”，但是他们一无所获。大脑中没有“愤怒模块”或“快乐中心”。相反，根据神经科学家卡里姆·卡萨姆和他的同事（Karim Kassam et al.，2013）的研究发现，不同的情绪拥有分布在大脑不同部位的独特“标记式”活动模式。通过训练演员再现特定情绪的“方法”，研究人员能够识别出与以下九种情绪相关的独特的大脑活动模式：厌恶、愤怒、恐惧、快乐、欲望、嫉妒、自豪、悲伤和羞耻。
p34.en: In the early days, people looked for brain “centres” to control specific emotions, but they didn't get anything. There's no "gry module" or "joy center" in the brain. On the contrary, research by neuroscientist Karim Qassam and his colleagues (Karim Kassam et al., 2013) found that different emotions have unique “marked” modes of activity distributed across different parts of the brain. Through the “methods” of training actors to recreate specific emotions, researchers can identify unique patterns of brain activity associated with nine types of emotions: aversion, anger, fear, happiness, desire, jealousy, pride, sorrow and shame.

p35.original: 9.10.6 自主神经系统在情绪中的作用
p35.en: 9.10.6 The role of the autonomous nervous system in emotions

p36.original: 情绪关乎全身，而不仅仅关乎大脑。当你的情绪激动起来时，你“传给心脏”（以及其他内脏器官）的信息会从你的大脑通过自主神经系统传到你的皮肤、肌肉和内脏器官（Levenson，1992）。副交感神经（parasumpathetic division）通常控制着愉悦的情绪。但当你受到惊吓或经历其他不愉快的情绪时，交感神经就会发挥作用（见表9-3）。
p36.en: Emotion is about the whole body, not just the brain. When you get emotional, your message of “transmission to the heart” (and other internal organs) is transmitted to your skin, muscle and internal organs from your brain through the autonomous nervous system (Levenson, 1992). Parasumpathic nerves usually control the mood of pleasure. However, when you are frightened or experience other unpleasant emotions, the sensory nerves work (see tables 9-3).

p37.original: 表9-3 与情绪相关的反应

p38.original: 假设你遇到了紧急情况（一辆超速的汽车正朝你开过来），你的大脑会通过交感神经系统传递的信息来提醒你的身体。沿着交感神经回路加速传递的信号会引起肾上腺释放应激激素。其他信号会让你的皮肤起鸡皮疙瘩、心跳加速、血压升高。同时，交感神经系统能引导某些血管收缩，将能量从胃肠转移到自主运动肌肉（这会让你有一种胃里打结的感觉）。
p38.en: Suppose you have an emergency, your brain will remind your body of the message from the sensory nervous system. An acceleration of the signal along the synaptic neuroreturn route would cause the adrenal release of the hormone. Other signals will give your skin a goosebump, an acceleration of the heart rate and a rise in blood pressure. At the same time, the synergetic nervous system can induce certain vascular contractions, shifting energy from the gastrointestinal to autonomous motion muscles (which gives you the feeling of a knot in the stomach).

p39.original: 在紧急情况消失后，副交感神经系统开始发挥作用，伴随的指令抵消了几分钟前的紧急命令。然而，在经历了强烈的情绪激活后，你可能会在一段时间内保持兴奋，因为激素继续在血液中循环着。如果这种情绪状况持续很长时间（就像士兵被派往战区一样），持续的应激反应最终会导致身体和精神上的障碍。
p39.en: After the emergency ceased to exist, the sub-conversation nervous system began to function, and the accompanying instructions offset the emergency orders of a few minutes ago. However, after intense emotional activation, you may remain excited for some time because hormones continue to circulate in the bloodstream. If this emotional situation lasts for a long time (as is the case with soldiers assigned to combat zones), sustained stress eventually leads to physical and mental impairments.

p41.original: 不，我们说的不只是爱。我们所有的情绪都依赖于体内产生的化学物质。对我们的情绪来说，最重要的是神经递质：血清素（serotonin）、肾上腺素（epinephrine）和去甲肾上腺素（norepinephrine）、催产素（oxytocin）和类固醇激素（steroid hormones）。
p41.en: No, we're not just talking about love. All our emotions depend on the chemicals that are produced in our bodies. For our emotions, the most important is neurotransmitters: serotonin, adrenaline, nerepinephrine, oxytocin and steroid hormones.

p42.original: 血清素与抑郁情绪有关。

p43.original: 肾上腺素是伴随恐惧的激素。
p43.en: Adrenalin is the hormone that goes with fear.

p44.original: 去甲肾上腺素会在愤怒时会分泌更多。
p44.en: Adrenalin is more likely to spread in anger.

p45.original: 催产素与依恋和人际吸引的感觉有关。
p45.en: The oxytocin is associated with feelings of attachment and interpersonal attraction.

p46.original: 类固醇激素（一些健身人群和其他运动员滥用的激素）也会对情绪产生强烈的影响。
p46.en: Steroid hormones (hormonals abused by some fitness groups and other athletes) can also have a strong emotional impact.

p47.original: 类固醇除了对肌肉有作用外，还可以作用于神经细胞，以改变它们的兴奋状态。这是身体对紧急情况的正常反应。但是，当长期摄入类固醇药物时，这些化学物质会使身体处于一种人为的应激状态。大脑回路，尤其是那些与觉醒、威胁、压力和强烈情绪相关的回路，会一直保持高度警惕。这可能会导致“类固醇癫狂”（Daly et al.，2003；Miller et al.，2002）。
p47.en: Steroids, in addition to their muscle effects, can also act on neurons to change their acupuncture. It's a normal physical response to emergencies. However, when ingestion of steroids is prolonged, these chemicals can place the body in an artificial stress. Brain loops, especially those associated with awakening, threats, stress and strong emotions, will remain highly vigilant. This could lead to “steroid epidemiology” (Daly et al., 2003); Miller et al., 2002).

p48.original: 与此同时，让我们来看看在短时间内保持一定水平的情绪唤醒是如何帮助你在运动、工作，甚至是下次心理学科目考试中获得最佳表现的。
p48.en: At the same time, let's see how maintaining a certain level of emotional awakening in a short period of time can help you achieve your best performance in sports, work and even the next psychological examination.

p49.original: 9.11 唤醒水平、成绩和倒U形曲线
p49.en: 9.11 Awakening Levels, Achievements and Rewinding U Curves

p51.original: 解释倒U形曲线，以及它与刺激寻求者之间的关系。
p51.en: Explain the reverse U-shaped curve and its relationship with the stimulator.

p52.original: 运动员总是想在比赛中“亢奋”，但是他们应该“亢奋”到什么程度呢？狂热的体育爱好者们可能会认为，提高唤醒水平就会使成绩提高，但这并不一定是真的。过度兴奋会让运动员“窒息”，进而导致成绩不佳。当你参加考试时也是一样的。在一定程度上，提高唤醒水平可以激励你学习，并帮你回忆所学的知识（还记得有研究表明情绪可以增强记忆吗）。遗憾的是，过高的唤醒水平会导致考试焦虑和成绩下降。
p52.en: Athletes always want to be “excited” in a game, but how much should they be “excited”? A fanatical sport lover may think that raising the level of awakening will lead to higher performance, but that is not necessarily true. Excessive excitement can “suffocate” athletes, which in turn leads to poor performance. It's the same when you take the exam. To some extent, higher levels of awakening can inspire you to learn and help you remember what you learned (remember any studies that show how emotions can enhance memory). Unfortunately, the high level of awakening could lead to an anxiety and a decline in performance in the examination.

p53.original: 这种唤醒水平和成绩之间的复杂关系已经在各种条件下的实验室动物和人类身上得到了验证。例如，在动物学习的实验中，想获得食物奖励的饥饿老鼠的完成任务表现曲线首先上升，然后随着唤醒水平的增加而下降。相同的模式也适用于各种情境下的人类，包括但不限于音乐表演、神经外科手术、体育比赛和期末考试。
p53.en: This complex relationship between the level of awakening and achievement has been validated in laboratory animals and in humans under various conditions. For example, in animal learning experiments, the performance curve of hungry mice seeking food rewards first rises and then declines as the level of awakening increases. The same model applies to human beings in all situations, including but not limited to musical performances, neurosurgery, sports competitions and final examinations.

p54.original: 心理学家称其为倒U形曲线（inverted U function，如此命名是因为该图类似于一个倒置的字母U，见图9-11）。
p54.en: Psychologists call it the reverse U curve (inverted U funcing), which is named because it resembles a reverse letter U, as shown in figures 9-11).

p55.original: 一般来说，获得最佳成绩时，会有一个最佳唤醒水平：太高或太低都会使成绩降低。想想看：你希望你的牙医在给你做根管治疗时感受到多大的压力呢？这就引出了第二个要点。
p55.en: Generally, there is an optimal level of awakening when the best results are achieved: too high or too low results are reduced. Think about it: How much pressure do you expect your dentist to feel when he's treating you with a tube? This leads to the second point.

p56.original: 最佳的唤醒水平因任务而异。从图中可以看出，相比复杂任务或需要深思熟虑并随着情况变化不断改变规划的任务，简单或经过充分演练的任务需要更多的唤醒水平才能取得最佳成绩。因此，欢呼和更高的唤醒水平可能更适合提高演员们的表现，而不适用于脑外科医生。
p56.en: The optimal level of awakening varies from mission to mission. As can be seen from the figure, a simple or well-rehearsed mission requires a higher level of awakening in order to achieve the best results than a complex mission or a task that requires careful consideration and constant change in planning as circumstances change. Therefore, cheering and higher levels of awakening may be better suited to improve the performance of actors than to brain surgeons.

p57.original: 当然，产生最佳唤醒水平所需的刺激量也因人而异。事实上，有些人似乎喜欢危险运动带来的刺激，如攀岩和跳伞（这些活动会让大多数人产生固定的唤醒水平）。马文·朱克曼（Marvin Zuckerman，2004）研究了他称之为刺激寻求者（sensation seeker）的一类人，他认为，这些人对高水平的刺激有生理需要。这种人有时被称为“肾上腺素瘾君子”。心理学家弗兰克·法利（Frank Farley）也将这类人称为“大T（寻求刺激）型”人格，他认为这类人在体育、商业、科学和艺术领域都很突出。法利曾说过，爱因斯坦就具有大T型“心理人格”（Munsey，2006）。研究表明，这背后的生物知识不仅涉及肾上腺素，还涉及大脑中分泌的多巴胺（Bevins，2001）。基于倒U形曲线，马库斯·马里奥塔在比赛日会到达曲线中的哪个位置呢？
p57.en: Of course, the amount of stimulus required to produce the best level of awakening also varies from person to person. In fact, some people seem to like the incentives provided by dangerous movements, such as rock climbing and jumping (these activities would create a fixed level of awakening for most people). Marvin Zuckerman, 2004, studied a group of people he called stimulators (sensation seeker), who, in his view, had biological needs for high levels of stimulation. This type of person is sometimes referred to as an "adrenal gland addict". The psychologist Frank Farley also referred to such persons as the “Big T” personality, which he considered prominent in the fields of sport, commerce, science and art. As Fari once said, Einstein has a large T-type “psychological personality” (Munsey, 2006). Research indicates that the biological knowledge behind this involves not only adrenaline but also dopamine in the brain (Bevens, 2001). On the basis of the reverse U-shaped curve, which position would Marcus Mariota reach in the curve on the day of the race?

p61.original: 不同的人似乎需要不同程度的情绪唤醒。马文·扎克曼认为，“刺激寻求者”对产生唤醒的刺激有着异常高的需要。除了对刺激的需要，刺激寻求者可能会更冲动，喜欢从事冒险行为，偏好新的体验，并且很容易感到无聊（Kohn et al.，1979；Malatesta et al.，1981；Zuckerman，1974）。
p61.en: Different people seem to need different levels of emotional awakening. Marvin Zackman argued that the “stimulant seeker” had an exceptionally high need for the stimulus to awaken. In addition to the need for stimulation, the motivation of the seeker may become more aggressive, prefer risky behaviour, prefer new experiences and be easily bored (Kohn et al., 1979); Malatesta et al., 1981; Zuckerman, 1974.

p97.original: 9.12 情绪理论：解决一些早期争论
p97.en: 9.12 Emotional theory: resolving some early disputes

p100.original: 让我们回到饥饿的熊的例子：假设有一天早上，你去上课的路上不幸遇到了这只饥饿的熊。我们打赌你会体验到恐惧的情绪。
p100.en: Let us return to the case of the hungry bear: assuming that one morning you were on your way to school and unfortunately met the hungry bear. We bet you'll experience fear.

p101.original: 但是，是什么样内在过程让你真正产生了恐惧的感觉呢？它是不是来自“啊，我目前有危险”？还是来自你对心跳加速和肠子撕裂的觉察？（而且，你可能也在想，为什么会有人关心情绪来自哪里？）
p101.en: But what kind of process does it really make you feel fear? Does it come from, "Ah, I'm in danger?" Or is it from your sense of heart rate acceleration and intestines torn? (And, you might also wonder, why does anyone care where the emotions come from? I don't think so.

p102.original: 对于最后一个问题：心理学家们长期以来一直在争论情绪、认知和身体反应之间的关系，这不仅是出于求知的好奇心，也是因为理解情绪是找到有效治疗某些情绪障碍的关键，例如，恐怖症和抑郁症，以及日常的愤怒、羡慕和嫉妒。例如，我们是否应该通过针对愤怒的想法来治疗愤怒？或者我们是否应该关注愤怒的行为？又或者关注伴随愤怒而来的本能反应？
p102.en: On the last question: Psychologists have long argued about the relationship between emotional, cognitive and physical responses, not only out of curiosity, but also because understanding emotions is key to finding effective treatment for certain emotional disorders, such as terror and depression, as well as daily anger, envy and jealousy. Should we, for example, treat anger by thinking about anger? Or should we focus on anger? Or are you concerned about the instincts of anger?

p103.original: 神经科学的最新发现帮助我们解决了一些长期的争论，这些争论围绕着生理、认知和情绪行为的相互作用展开（Forgas，2008）。让我们简要地看看这些争论，以及新的观点是如何解决它们的。
p103.en: The latest findings of neuroscience have helped us to resolve some of the long-standing disputes surrounding the interaction of physical, cognitive and emotional behaviour (Forgas, 2008). Let us briefly look at these arguments and at how new ideas have addressed them.

p104.original: 9.12.1 我们的情绪体验来自身体反应吗
p104.en: 9.12.1 Our emotional experience comes from physical reactions?

p105.original: 在心理学发展的早期，也就是一个多世纪以前，威廉·詹姆斯教导我们，身体的感觉是我们体验的基础。“我们难过是因为我们哭了，生气是因为我们愤怒了，害怕是因为我们颤抖了。”詹姆斯如是说（1890/1950，p.1006）。至于你对熊的反应，詹姆斯认为，你不会因为害怕而逃跑，而是因为逃跑而感到害怕。虽然这一说法表面上看起来很荒谬，但詹姆斯不是傻瓜。他知道情绪不仅仅是感觉。他真正想说的是一些很有道理的东西，即情绪需要认知和身体感觉相结合，而身体感觉就是体验。用詹姆斯（1884）的话来说就是：
p105.en: In the early years of psychological development, more than a century ago, William James taught us that the feeling of body is the basis of our experience. “We're sad because we're crying, angry because we're angry, afraid because we're shaking. As James said (1890/1950, p. 1006). As for your reaction to the bear, James believes that you are not afraid to run away, but rather afraid to escape. Although this statement appears absurd, James is not a fool. He knows emotions are not just feelings. What he really wants to say is something that makes sense, that emotions need to be combined with cognitive and physical feelings, and that physical feelings are experiences. In the words of James:

p106.original: 如果没有看到熊之后的身体状态，接下来将只是纯粹的认知而已，苍白、无色、缺乏情感温度。当我们看到这只熊时，我们可能会判断现在最好是逃跑、忍受攻击或抗争，但我们实际上不会感到害怕或愤怒。
p106.en: If the health of the bear is not seen, then it will be purely cognitive, pale, colourless and lacking emotional temperature. When we look at this bear, we may judge that it is best to flee, endure attacks or fight, but we will not actually be afraid or angry.

p107.original: 这一观点由丹麦心理学家卡尔·兰格（Carl Lange）同时提出，后来被称为詹姆斯-兰格理论（James-Lange theory）。
p107.en: This view was also presented by the Danish psychologist Carl Lange, later known as James-Lange theory.

p108.original: 9.12.2 我们的情绪体验来自认知吗
p108.en: Is our emotional experience from cognitive?

p109.original: 其他一些科学家，尤其是沃尔特·坎农（Walter Cannon）和菲利普·巴德（Philip Bard），反对称，我们行为或内部器官的生理变化发生得太慢，无法解释瞬间的情绪反应，如我们在面临危险时的情绪反应。他们还反对说，我们的身体反应变化不够多，不足以解释人类所有的情绪类型。在他们看来，对一个场景（如饥饿的熊）的认知评价，能同时产生情绪体验（恐惧）和身体反应（逃跑），这被称为坎农-巴德理论（Eannon-Bard theory）。
p109.en: Other scientists, especially Walter Cannon and Philip Bard, object that the physical changes in our behaviour or internal organs are too slow to explain the emotional reactions of the moment, such as our emotional reactions in the face of danger. They also objected to the fact that our physical response had not changed enough to explain all the emotional types of humankind. In their view, a cognitive assessment of a scene (such as a hungry bear) can produce both emotional experiences (fear) and physical reactions (escape), known as the Cannon-Bard theory (Eannon-Bard theory).

p110.original: 哪一方是正确的？ 事实证明，每个理论都包含一部分事实真相。一方面，现代神经科学已经证实了身体状态可以影响我们的情绪，就像詹姆斯-兰格理论所认为的那样（LeDoux，1996）。事实上，你可能已经注意到你自己的身体状态是如何影响情绪的，例如，当你喝了太多咖啡后会感到焦躁不安，或者当你饿了会变得暴躁。同样，精神类药物，如酒精、尼古丁或百忧解也会影响大脑的生理状况，从而改变我们的情绪。
p110.en: Which side is right? Each theory has proved to contain a part of the truth. On the one hand, modern neuroscience has shown that the state of health can affect our emotions, as the James-Langer theory suggests (LeDoux, 1996). In fact, you may have noticed how your physical state affects emotions, for example, when you drink too much coffee, or when you're hungry. Likewise, psychopharmaceutical drugs, such as alcohol, nicotine or Prozac, can affect the physiological state of the brain, thereby changing our emotions.

p111.original: 詹姆斯-兰格理论的其他证据来自两个发现：（1）无意识的情绪处理回路，（2）大脑记住与情绪事件相关的身体状态。这些记忆就是我们之前提到的躯体标记（Damasio，1994；Niedenthal，2007）。所以，当你看到熊笨拙地向你走来时，你的大脑很快就会触发之前在危险情况下所经历的生理反应的身体记忆。这个躯体标记假说有效地驳斥了沃尔特·坎农的学说，即身体的变化发生得太慢而不能引发我们的情绪体验，因为情绪的躯体标记根植于大脑本身。
p111.en: Other evidence of the James-Langer theory comes from two findings: (1) unconscious emotional treatment circuits, and (2) the brain remembers the physical state associated with emotional events. These memories are the body markers we mentioned earlier (Damasio, 1994); Niedenthal, 2007. So, when you see the bear coming to you in a clumsy way, your brain will soon trigger the physical memory of the physical reaction you experienced in a dangerous situation. This body marking hypothesis effectively refutes Walter Cannon's theory that changes in body are too slow to trigger our emotional experience, because the body marking of emotion is embedded in the brain itself.

p112.original: 另外，情绪也可以被有意识或无意识的情绪系统检测到的外部线索所激发，这也支持了坎农-巴德理论。因此，情绪可能来自有意识的思考（如当你为考试烦恼时）或无意识的记忆（如当你看到曾经让你感到恶心的食物时）。顺便说一句，如今认知心理学家认为，抑郁和恐惧反应都是由无意识情绪系统的条件反应造成的。
p112.en: In addition, emotions can be stimulated by external clues detected by conscious or unconscious emotional systems, which also underpins the Canon-Bad theory. So emotions can come from conscious thinking (e.g. when you're upset about the exam) or unconscious memories (e.g. when you see food that once made you sick). By the way, today cognitive psychologists believe that both depression and fear responses are caused by a conditional response of an unconscious emotional system.

p114.original: 正如我们提到的，你可以通过思考自己的问题和恐惧来让自己变得情绪化，任何有过“考试焦虑症”的学生都可以证明这一点。你越是想考试不及格的可怕后果，你的焦虑感就越强烈。“体验派”演员，如已故的马龙·白兰度（Marlon Brando），长期以来一直在利用认知的力量让自己在舞台上感受到真实的情绪。他们通过回忆自己经历过的事情来表达自己想要表达的情绪，如悲伤、快乐或愤怒。
p114.en: As we have mentioned, you can make yourself emotional by thinking about your problems and fears, as can be demonstrated by any student who has had “test anxiety”. The more you want the terrible consequences of failing, the more anxious you are. “Empirical” actors, such as the late Marlon Brando, have long used the power of awareness to make themselves feel real on stage. They express the emotions they want to express by remembering what they have experienced, such as grief, happiness or anger.

p115.original: 斯坦利·沙赫特（Stanley Schachter，1971）的双因素理论（two-factor theory）给认知在情绪中的作用增加了一个转折。他的理论表明，我们感受到的情绪取决于我们对以下两个方面的评估：（1）我们内在的身体状态，（2）我们对情境的知觉。然而，他发现，当这两个因素发生冲突时，奇怪的事情就会发生（就像他们在一项经典的情绪研究中所做的那样）。有进取心的学生可能想要重复下面这一研究，为他们的浪漫生活增添情趣。
p115.en: Stanley Schachter, 1971's double-factor theory added a turning point to the role of cognitiveism in emotions. His theory shows that the emotions we feel depend on our assessment of (1) our inner state of health, and (2) our perception of the situation. However, he found that when these two factors clash, strange things happen (as they did in a classic emotional study). Promulgated students may want to repeat the following study to add to their romantic life.

p116.original: 一位迷人的女性研究人员站在一座桥的桥头附近，然后她走近刚过桥的男性，要求他们回答一份问卷。在一种情况下，是一座安全坚固的钢筋混凝土桥；在另外一种情况下，是一座横跨峡谷的摇摇晃晃的吊桥。选择后者的目的是为了刺激人们身体上的唤醒。研究人员假装是在研究风景对创造力的影响，让这些男性写一个关于一幅画的简短故事。她还告知这些男性，如果想了解更多关于这项研究的信息，可以打电话给她。
p116.en: A charming female researcher stood near the bridge head, then approached the male who had just crossed the bridge and asked them to answer a questionnaire. In one case, it is a secure and solid concrete bridge; In another case, it was a swinging suspension bridge across the canyon. The latter was chosen to stimulate physical awakening. Researchers pretend to be studying the impact of landscapes on creativity, allowing these men to write a short story about a painting. She also informed the men that she could call if they wished to learn more about the study.

p117.original: 结果正如我们预测的那样，那些刚刚走过摇摇晃晃的吊桥的男性（想必是在过桥的过程中产生更多的生理唤醒）创作的故事比那些走过坚固的桥的男性创作的故事包含更多的性想象（这是根据主题统觉测验中有经验的解读者判断的）。顺便说一句，走摇摇晃晃的吊桥的男性打电话给女研究员（为获得更多信息）的人数，是走坚固的桥的人数的四倍。实验者得出的结论是，那些走过摇摇晃晃的吊桥的人把他们不断增加的唤醒水平归因于对女研究员的情感吸引（Dutton & Aron，1974）。
p117.en: As a result, as we predicted, the stories of men who had just walked through the swinging suspension bridge (and, presumably, produced more biological awakenings during the crossing) were more sexual than those of men who had come across the strong bridge (as judged by experienced readers in the subject-based generalization test). By the way, the number of men who call female researchers (for more information) on the swinging bridge is four times the number of people who walk on the strong bridge. The experiment concluded that those who walked through the swinging suspension bridge attributed their increasing level of awakening to the emotional attraction of female researchers (Dutton & Aron, 1974).

p118.original: 在你走过摇摇晃晃的吊桥来寻找生命中的挚爱之前，我们必须警告你，虽然无数次测试和实验都支持双因素理论，但这只有在特定的条件下才奏效（Leventhal & Tomarken，1986；Sinclair et al.，1994）。在通常情况下，外部事件证实了生理唤醒告诉我们的东西，这不需要太详细的解释。例如，当你闻到难闻的气味时会感到恶心，或者看到老朋友时会感到高兴。只有当我们因不太明显的原因（如运动、热、药物或摇晃的桥）而经历生理唤醒时，我们才会对生理唤醒的起源感到困惑。这种错误归因最可能发生在复杂的环境中，即当许多刺激都在争夺我们的注意力，或者环境中存在对我们的生理唤醒有误导的信息时（见图9-12）。
p118.en: We must warn you that, while numerous tests and experiments support the dual-factor theory, this works only under certain conditions (Leventhal & Tomarken, 1986; ) Sinclair et al., 1994. As a rule, external events confirm what the physiological awakenings tell us, which does not require too detailed an explanation. For example, you get sick when you smell bad, or you get happy when you see old friends. Only when we experience physical awakening for less obvious reasons (such as sports, heat, drugs or shaking bridges) will we be confused about the origins of physical awakening. This error is most likely to occur in complex environments, where many incentives compete for our attention or where there is misleading information about our physiological awakening (see figures 9-12).

p120.original: 对球芽甘蓝的积极感受

p121.original: 虽然很多人不喜欢吃球芽甘蓝，但假设你非常喜欢它，因为你去奶奶家的时候她总是在做球芽甘蓝，你也很喜欢和奶奶在一起的时光。请指出三种情绪理论（见图9-12，詹姆斯-兰格理论、坎农-巴德理论或沙赫特的双因素理论）中的哪一种最能解释你对球芽甘蓝的积极感受，并解释原因。
p121.en: Although many people don't like it, assuming you like it because when you go to Grandma's, she always makes it, and you like the time with Grandma. Please indicate which of the three emotional theories (see figures 9-12, James-Lange theory, Cannon-Bad theory or Shaht's double-factor theory) best explain your positive feelings about the ball sprouts and explain why.

p122.original: 9.13 我们对自己的情绪有多少控制力
p122.en: 9.13 How much control do we have over our emotions?

p124.original: 描述情绪智力的组成部分，并解释它是否可以被习得。
p124.en: Describe the mental component and explain whether it can be learned.

p125.original: 处理情绪的能力在很多职业中都很重要。例如，医生、护士、消防员、警察和临床心理学家都必须能够安慰他人，但在面对残疾和死亡时，又必须要“保持专业距离”。情绪控制也可以用来掩饰或改变你在社交场合的感觉。所以，如果你不喜欢一位教授，最好隐藏自己的真实情绪。即使在休闲活动中（如打扑克），如果你能控制自己的情绪反应，那么你也会玩得很好。这种技能是可以学习的，还是与生俱来的呢？
p125.en: The ability to deal with emotions is important in many occupations. For example, doctors, nurses, firefighters, police officers and clinical psychologists must be able to comfort others, but in the face of disability and death, they must “maintain professional distance”. Emotional control can also be used to mask or change your feelings in social settings. So if you don't like a professor, you better hide your true emotions. Even in leisure activities (e.g. poker), if you can control your emotional reaction, you can play well. Is this a skill that can be learned, or is it born?

p128.original: 神经学家理查德·戴维森（Richard Davidson）发现，人们都有一个典型的“情绪风格”，这意味着每个人的情绪反应不同，就像每个人的人格特质不同一样（Davidson & Begley，2012；Winerman，2012）。但对心理学家彼得·沙洛维（Peter Salovey）和约翰·梅耶（John Mayer，1990）来说，区分人们不同情绪的最有趣的方式涉及一组被其称为情商（emotional intelligence，EI）的能力。他们指出，这种能力不是简单的快乐、乐观或高自尊（Salovey & Grewal，2005；Mayer et al.，2008）。相反，他们认为情商应该是以下四种能力的组合。
p128.en: Neurologist Richard Davidson found that people all have a typical “emotional style”, which means that each person's emotional reaction is different, just as each person's personality is different (Davison & Begley, 2012); Winerman, 2012. However, for the psychologist Peter Salovey and John Mayer, the most interesting way to distinguish people from different emotions relates to a set of capabilities that they call emotional intelligence. They noted that such capabilities were not simply pleasure, optimism or high self-esteem (Salovey & Grewal, 2005); Mayer et al., 2008). Rather, they believe that intelligence should be a combination of four capacities:

p129.original: 感知情绪——发现和解读自己和他人情绪的能力。
p129.en: Sensory sentiment - the ability to discover and interpret one's feelings and those of others.

p130.original: 利用情绪——利用情绪思考和解决问题的能力。
p130.en: Use emotions — use emotional thinking and problem solving.

p131.original: 理解情绪——理解情绪之间复杂关系的能力，例如，悲伤和愤怒之间的关系，或者为何两个人对同一事件有不同的情绪反应。
p131.en: The ability to understand emotions — the complex relationship between emotions, for example, between grief and anger, or why two people react differently to the same event.

p132.original: 管理情绪——调节自己情绪并影响他人情绪的能力。
p132.en: Managing emotions - the ability to regulate one's emotions and influence others' emotions.

p133.original: 正如沙洛维和梅耶所指出的，那些高情商的人不仅能调节自己和他人的情绪，而且还能控制自己的负面情绪，尽量避免用不恰当的方式表达自己的冲动。
p133.en: As Shalom and Meyer have pointed out, those who are highly interested not only can regulate themselves and others ' emotions, but also can control their negative emotions and avoid expressing their impulses in an inappropriate manner.

p134.original: 但我们能像测试传统智商那样评估情商吗？
p134.en: But can we evaluate intelligence like traditional IQ tests?

p136.original: 事实证明，情商在人类生命的早期就令人吃惊地表现了出来，斯坦福大学心理学家沃尔特·米歇尔（Walter Mischel）独创的“棉花糖测验”确实可以测量情商。丹尼尔·戈尔曼（Daniel Goleman，1995）描述了这一过程：
p136.en: It turns out that the intelligence has been striking in the early days of human life, and that the “margin sugar test” created by the University of Stanford psychologist Walter Mischel does measure the intelligence. Daniel Goleman, 1995 describes this process:

p137.original: 想象一下，你是一个四岁的小孩，有人向你询问：如果你愿意等到他出去办事回来，你可以得到两块棉花糖作为奖励；如果你不能等到那个时候，你只能拥有一块，但是你现在就可以拥有它。
p137.en: Imagine you're a four-year-old kid, and you're asked: if you want to wait until he gets back to work, you can get two marshmallows as a reward; If you can't wait until then, you can only have one piece, but you can have it now.

p138.original: 年幼的孩子们对摆在他们面前的来自一块棉花糖的诱惑究竟是如何做出反应的？戈尔曼继续说：
p138.en: How do young children react to the temptation of a marshmallow before them? Gorman goes on:

p139.original: 一些四岁的孩子能够等待15～20分钟，直到实验者回来。为了在挣扎中控制自己，他们要么捂住眼睛，以免盯着棉花糖，要么把头枕在胳膊里，跟自己说话、唱歌，用手和脚玩游戏，甚至想睡觉。这些勇敢的学龄前儿童得到了两块棉花糖作为奖励。但是，其他更易冲动的孩子，几乎总是在实验人员一离开房间执行“任务”的几秒内，就抓起了这一块棉花糖。
p139.en: Some four-year-olds can wait 15 to 20 minutes until the experimenter returns. In order to control themselves in their struggle, they either cover their eyes so that they do not stare at marshmallows, or lay their heads in their arms, speak to themselves, sing, play games with their hands and feet, or even want to sleep. These brave pre-school children were rewarded with two marshmallows. However, other, more impulsive children almost always caught this marshmallow as soon as the experimenter left the room to perform his “task”.

p140.original: 这些结果表明，情商的差异确实在人们小时候就表现出来了。但它们是天生的吗？它们会持续存在吗？
p140.en: These results show that the differences in intelligence do occur when people are young. But are they born? Will they last?

p142.original: 当这些孩子在青春期和40多岁被追踪时，棉花糖测验惊人的预测能力显现了出来。从群体上看，那些克制住自己想吃一块棉花糖的人在青少年时期的所有方面都做得更好。他们变得更加独立，处理人际关系更加高效，成了更好的学生，能够更好地应对困难和压力。相比之下，那些屈服于诱惑的孩子，其青少年时期生活的特点是人际关系不佳、害羞、固执和优柔寡断。他们对自己的评价也更低，不信任他人，很容易被挫折激怒。在学术领域，他们对学校不感兴趣。更让人惊讶的是，他们发现棉花糖测验的成绩与SAT（美国高中毕业生学术能力水平考试）分数之间存在关联：那些在四岁时能够延迟满足的孩子，在SAT考试中的平均得分比那些当时只拿到一块棉花糖的同龄人高出210分。最后，新的研究表明两组被试的大脑扫描成像也有明显的差异（Casey et al.，2011；Chamberlin，2011）。
p142.en: When these children are tracked in adolescence and in their late 40s, the ability to predict the marshmallow test is striking. From a group perspective, those who restrain themselves from eating a piece of marshmallow do better in all aspects of adolescence. They have become more independent and efficient in dealing with interpersonal relations, becoming better students and better able to cope with difficulties and pressures. In contrast, children who succumb to temptation are characterized by poor interpersonal relationships, shyness, stubbornness and indecisiveness. They also rated themselves lower, distrusted and easily provoked frustration. In the academic sphere, they are not interested in schools. Even more surprising, they found a correlation between the performance of the marshmallow test and the scores of the SAT (Academies of Academic Competencies for American High School Graduates): the average score in the SAT examination was 210 points higher than those of those who had received only one piece of marshmallow at the time. Finally, new studies suggest that there are also significant differences in the scan images of two test-tested brain (Casey et al., 2011); Chamberlin, 2011.

p143.original: 当然，虽然棉花糖测验的有效性仅限于幼儿。但其他更复杂的研究方法已被开发出来用于较年长的儿童和成年人（见图9-13）。
p143.en: Of course, although the effectiveness of the marshmallow test is limited to young children. However, other more complex research methods have been developed for use in older children and adults (see figures 9-13).

p144.original: 图9-13 一项情绪智力测试的示例
p144.en: Figure 9-13 Example of an emotional intelligence test

p145.original: 注：这里展示的是一个类似于梅耶-沙洛维-库索情商测试的项目。被试需要根据照片中人物的情绪状态点击每个量表上的数字。
p145.en: Note: A project similar to the Meyer-Salowy-Cuso intelligence test is presented here. The test involves clicking on the number on each scale according to the emotional state of the person in the photograph.

p146.original: 例如，梅耶-沙洛维-库索情商测试似乎测试了基本相同的能力，预测男性青少年的异常行为、大学生的社会关系满意度、成年人的婚姻满意度和工作成就（Salovey & Grewal，2005）。
p146.en: For example, the Meye-Salowi-Cuso intelligence test appears to have tested essentially the same capabilities for predicting abnormal behaviour among male adolescents, satisfaction with social relations among university students, marriage satisfaction among adults and work achievement (Salovey & Grewal, 2005).

p147.original: 但是，约翰·梅耶（1999）警告说，情商测试并不总是恒定不变的。数据显示，有些人随着慢慢地成熟会发生明显的变化。我们也不应该认为情商可以取代传统的智商。梅耶说，相反，情商仅仅是另一个变量，它可以帮助我们更好地理解人与人之间的差异。
p147.en: However, John Mayer (1999) warned that intelligence testing was not always constant. The data show that some people change significantly as they mature slowly. Nor should we consider intelligence as a substitute for traditional IQ. Meyer said, on the contrary, intelligence is just another variable that can help us better understand the differences between people.

p148.original: 9.13.4 情商的先天性和后天培养
p148.en: 9.13.4 Inheritance and acquired culture of emotional intelligence

p149.original: 现在，让我们回到开始讨论的问题：情商是由先天遗传决定的，还是由后天经验培养的？
p149.en: Now, let's return to the question that began: is the relationship determined by birth or by the experience of the day after?

p150.original: 由约瑟夫·杜拉克（Joseph Durlak）领导的一个由心理学家组成的研究团队对200多个旨在提升情商的学校项目进行了系统性总结，他们也将这些项目称为社会和情绪学习（Sociel and Emotional Learning，SEL，Durlak & Weissberg，2011；Durlak et al，2011）。这些项目侧重于人际问题解决、目标设定、压力管理、同理心和决策。所有这些都涉及具体的指导和学生的积极参与。在这些活动中，老师会模拟一个事件，如游乐场冲突，然后让学生参与练习。研究结果值得一提：
p150.en: A research team of psychologists led by Joseph Durlak conducted a systematic summary of over 200 school projects aimed at promoting intelligence, which they also referred to as social and emotional learning (Sociel and Emotional Learning, SEL, Durlak & Weissberg, 2011); Durlak et al., 2011. These projects focus on interpersonal issues, targeting, stress management, common sense and decision-making. All of this involves specific guidance and the active participation of students. At these events, teachers simulate an event, such as a playground conflict, and then involve students in practice. The results of the study are worth mentioning:

p151.original: SEL项目显著提升了学生的社交和情绪技能、学生对自己和学校的态度，以及他们的课外和课堂行为。SEL项目还显著减少了学生的问题行为，如课堂不当行为和攻击性行为，也减少了他们所表现出的焦虑、抑郁和压力等情绪困扰症状。
p151.en: The SEL project has significantly improved students ' social and emotional skills, students ' attitudes towards themselves and their schools, and their extra-curricular and classroom behaviour. The SEL project has also significantly reduced students ' problem behaviour, such as classroom misconduct and aggressive behaviour, as well as the symptoms of emotional distress, depression and stress that they display.

p152.original: 一个特别重要的发现是，这些进步并不是以牺牲学业为代价的。他们继续写道：
p152.en: A particularly important finding is that these advances are not at the expense of schooling. They continue to write:

p153.original: 参与SEL项目还与成绩测试分数及学校成绩的提高有关，大家的学术成就分数上升了11%……此外，在小学、初中和高中，城市、农村和郊区的学校，以及为种族和文化多样性学生提供服务的学校里，学生展现出的成效都是积极的。
p153.en: Participation in the SEL project is also related to the improvement of achievement scores and school achievement, which rose by 11 per cent. In addition, students show positive results in primary, lower secondary and upper secondary schools, in urban, rural and suburban schools, and in schools serving students with ethnic and cultural diversity.

p154.original: 由此得出的结论是，尽管情绪有时会失控，但我们并不是只能受情绪摆布。情绪理解和控制是可以习得的技能（Clifton & Myers，2005）。
p154.en: The conclusion is that, while emotions sometimes get out of hand, we are not left to be guided by emotions. Emotional understanding and control are skills that can be learned (Clifton & Myers, 2005).

p155.original: 然而，一些反对者指出，情绪控制可能有不好的一面。就像有些人因放任自己的情绪（尤其是负面情绪）而陷入麻烦一样，另一些人则把情绪控制推向了另一个极端。他们变得十分警惕，以至于他们从不表达情绪、幽默或内心的不快。研究还表明，过度控制情绪会干扰情绪性事件的记忆（Carpenter，2000；Richards & Gross，2000）。在我们启动一个提倡情绪控制的科研项目之前，或许我们应该考虑一下这种训练对那些已经过度控制情绪的人会产生什么影响。事实上，研究表明，情绪健康的人知道如何控制和表达自己的情绪，以及何时该这样做（Bonanno et al.，2004）。
p155.en: However, some opponents pointed out that emotional control might be a bad side. Just as some people are in trouble for letting their emotions (especially negative ones), others are pushing emotional control to another extreme. They have become so vigilant that they never express emotions, humor or impatience within themselves. Research also shows that over-control of emotions can interfere with memory of emotional events (Carpenter, 2000); Richards & Gross, 2000. Before we launch a scientific project to promote emotional control, perhaps we should consider what impact such training will have on those who have over-controlled their emotions. Indeed, research shows that people who are emotionally healthy know how to control and express their emotions and when to do so (Bonanno et al., 2004).

p156.original: 9.13.5 释放情绪：一个危险的神话

p157.original: 专家们一致认为，大众不愿放弃一些危险的关于发泄愤怒的错误想法，这一过程也被称为宣泄。许多人认为“压抑”情绪是情绪爆发的原因，但这种看法与事实不符。这么做也是情商低的表现！事实上，发泄一下怒气，如扔掉一个咖啡杯，“把坏情绪从你的身体里赶出去”，可能只会带来最短暂的满足感，却会延长愤怒的时间。因为这相当于练习如何发怒，它实际上会让你在下次更有可能有一个爆炸性的反应（Tavris，1989，1995）。
p157.en: The experts agreed that the public was reluctant to give up some of the dangerous misconceptions of anger, a process that was also referred to as excretion. Many consider “pressure” to be the cause of the outbreak, but this view is not consistent with reality. It's also a sign of a low level of love! In fact, a little anger, such as throwing away a coffee cup and “exploiting bad feelings out of your body”, may only bring the shortest sense of satisfaction, but it will prolong the time of anger. As this is tantamount to practicing anger, it will actually make you more likely to have an explosive reaction next time (Tavris, 1989, 1995).

p158.original: 一个更理智、更安全的策略是将情绪留给自己，至少在你的愤怒平息之前不要发泄出来。你可以更理智地看待你真正想抱怨的事物，以及如何解决这个问题（Tavris，1989，1995）。通常，化解紧张和愤怒的局面只需你与令你感到愤怒的人交流一下事情本身和你的感受而已。
p158.en: A more rational and safer strategy is to leave your emotions to yourself, at least not to vent your anger until your anger has subsided. You can look more rationally at what you really want to complain about and how to solve it (Tavris, 1989, 1995). Normally, you just have to share the matter and your feelings with someone who makes you angry.

p159.original: 心理学很有用 检测欺骗

p160.original: 人们在说谎的时候掩饰自己的情绪是容易还是困难？你可能会认为，当某人没有“直视你的眼睛”或紧张不安时，你就能发现对方在欺骗你。如果你认为事情如此简单，你就会成为撒谎高手的首要目标。事实上，大多数人都不擅长识别谎言或发现真相。
p160.en: Is it easy or difficult for people to hide their emotions while lying? You might think that when someone doesn't look at your eyes or get nervous, you can see that the other person is cheating on you. If you think it's so simple, you'll be the first target of a liar. In fact, most people are not very good at identifying lies or finding the truth.

p161.original: 研究谎言的专家发现，某些特定的非语言线索是谎言的最佳标志。故意欺骗我们的人可能会“泄露”不受控制的欺骗的非言语信号。知道如何解读这些线索可以帮助你判断卖家是否在撒谎，你的医生是否在隐瞒一些坏消息，或者一个政客是否在隐瞒真相。但是，请记住，对谎言的研究基于不确定性，而非确定性。这些研究都还未达到科学的精确要求。尽管如此，我们仍然可以为某些情境提供一些有用的信息，在这些情境下，即使是一点点帮助也可能比没有要好（Adelson，2004；DePaulo et al.，2003）。
p161.en: The experts who studied the lie found that certain specific non-verbal clues were the best sign of the lie. Those who deliberately deceive us may “discover” the non-verbal signals of uncontrolled deception. Knowing how to interpret these clues helps you judge whether the seller is lying, whether your doctor is hiding some bad news, or whether a politician is hiding the truth. However, remember that the study of lies is based on uncertainty rather than certainty. None of these studies meet the scientific precision requirements. Nevertheless, we can still provide useful information in certain situations where even a little help can be better than nothing (Adelson, 2004); DePaulo et al., 2003.

p162.original: 谎言需要认知上的努力。有些谎言包括提供虚假信息，例如，一个二手车卖家告诉你一辆破车运转良好。在这种情况下，掩盖真相需要一些认知上的努力。这可能会导致注意力高度集中（明显的表现有瞳孔扩大）、讲话时停顿的时间更长（谨慎选择词语），以及更多受限的动作和手势（试图避免“泄露”真相）。
p162.en: Lies require cognitive effort. Some of the lies included the provision of false information, such as a second-hand car seller who told you that a car was working well. Under such circumstances, the concealment of the truth requires some cognitive effort. This may lead to a high concentration of attention (manifestly manifested by the expansion of pupils), longer pauses in speech (precautionary choice of words) and more restricted movements and gestures (in an attempt to avoid “discovering” the truth).

p163.original: 说谎者会重复歪曲的细节。对犯罪供词的分析表明，故意歪曲事实的人倾向于重复他们篡改过的故事的细节（Dingfelder，2004c）。
p163.en: The liar repeats the distorted details. An analysis of the confession of guilt shows that those who deliberately distort the facts tend to repeat the details of the stories that they tampered with (Dingfelder, 2004c).

p164.original: 经常说真话的骗子。事实上，“直视你的眼睛”的能力是一个很好的判断说谎指标，但仅限于和通常讲真话的人打交道时。当这些人撒谎时，他们通常会表现为目光转移，眨眼减少（表示注意力集中在其他地方），以及较少微笑。但是，要小心那些老练的说谎者，当他们正在讲一个虚假的谎言时，仍可以直视你。
p164.en: He's a liar who always tells the truth. In fact, the ability to “look at your eyes” is a good indicator of a lie, but only when dealing with people who usually speak the truth. When these people lie, they usually show a shift in their eyes, a decrease in their blinking (which means that they focus on other places) and a decrease in their smile. But beware of those who lie with a skill, and when they are telling a lie, they may still look at you.

p165.original: 生理唤醒可能意味着对真相的抑制。当一个谎言是为了隐藏真相，而不是单纯地编造一个故事（就像一个扑克高手拿着一张同花顺牌时所做的那样）时，说谎者可能会在身体上和行为上变得更加兴奋和活跃。姿势的变化、语言错误、紧张的手势（如梳理头发或抚摸脸）和耸肩（好像是为了消除谎言）会表现得很明显。相反，当说谎者热情地说了一个弥天大谎时，唤醒水平可能不是一个好的指标。
p165.en: Physical awakening may mean inhibition of the truth. When a lie is designed to hide the truth, rather than simply fabricate a story (as a poker player does when he holds a flower-like card), the liar may become more excited and active physically and in behaviour. Changes in postures, linguistic errors, stressful gestures (such as combing hair or touching face) and shrugging (as if to remove lies) are evident. On the contrary, awakening levels may not be a good indicator when the liar says a great lie enthusiastically.

p166.original: 注意身体和面部。脸比身体更容易控制，所以，说谎者可能会努力保持一副“扑克脸”，而忘记了控制身体的线索。因此，一个聪明的侦探可能会专注于说话者的身体动作：它们是否有节奏？他们是故意的吗？手的动作是流畅的还是紧张的？
p166.en: Watch your body and face. Faces are easier to control than bodies, so liars may try to keep a “poker face” and forget the clues to control bodies. So, a smart detective might focus on the physical actions of the talking person: do they have a rhythm? Did they do it on purpose? Are your hands flowing or nervous?

p167.original: 文化影响了我们区分真理和谎言的方式。在我们的文化中，我们更能准确地发现说谎者。因此，即使来自另一种文化的人没有撒谎，我们也更可能认为他们在撒谎。例如，一项研究发现，约旦人在说话时通常比美国人更活跃，美国人可能会错误地以为这是“紧张”的表现，并认定约旦人在撒谎（Bond & Atoum，2000；Dingfelder2004c）。
p167.en: Culture has influenced the way we distinguish between truth and lies. In our culture, we are better able to find liars. Thus, even if people from another culture do not lie, we are more likely to think that they are lying. For example, a study found that Jordanians are usually more active than Americans, who may mistakenly believe that this is a “strike” and find Jordanians lying (Bond & Atoum, 2000); Dingfelder2004c.

p168.original: 眼睛比嘴巴更能说明问题。骗子的眼神有时会出卖他们，尤其当他们在用常见的社交欺骗手段试图让自己看起来开心或愉快时，实际上他们并不开心。虽然我们的注意力可能更自然地集中在一个作为快乐或娱乐标志的微笑上，但其实嘴巴比眼睛周围的肌肉更容易被操纵。这个微笑是真的吗？只有在真正的微笑中，眼部肌肉才会使眼睛两侧的皮肤产生皱纹。你可以通过“试一试”栏目中的测验来测试自己分辨真假微笑的能力。
p168.en: The eyes are more telling than the mouth. Liars sometimes sell their eyes, especially when they try to look happy or happy with common social deception. While our attention may be more naturally focused on a smile as a sign of pleasure or entertainment, it is in fact easier to manipulate the mouth than the muscles around the eyes. Is this smile real? Only in a true smile can eye muscles wrinkle skins from both sides of the eye. You can use the test in the "Try to Try" column to test your ability to discern the true smile.

p169.original: 记住：上述这些都不是撒谎的标志，即使是专家也会犯错。专家们说，有效检测欺骗的关键是长期观察一个人的行为。如果没有反复观察的机会，你就很难判断一个人是否诚实（Marsh，1988）。
p169.en: Remember, these are not signs of lies, even experts make mistakes. Experts said that the key to effective detection of fraud was to observe a person's behaviour over a long period of time. Without the opportunity to observe repeatedly, it is difficult to judge whether a person is honest (Marsh, 1988).

p170.original: 试一试 眼睛有魔力
p170.en: Try it. It's magic in the eyes.

p171.original: 当人们对你微笑时，你能辨别出他们是否出于真心吗？真心的微笑不仅仅要用嘴，而是需要动用整个面部，尤其是眼睛。真正的微笑与假笑是不同的，主要不同在眼睛周围。具体来说，当我们感到真正的喜悦或欢笑时，眼轮匝肌会使眼睛周围的皮肤产生皱纹。
p171.en: When people smile at you, can you tell if they're sincere? A genuine smile is not just a mouth, but a whole face, especially an eye. Real smiles are different from fake smiles, mainly around the eyes. Specifically, when we feel real joy or laughter, eye muscles create wrinkles in the skin around our eyes.

p172.original: 考虑到这一点，观察一下你周围的笑脸，看看你能否分辨出哪个是真正的微笑，哪个是被动的微笑。
p172.en: With that in mind, look around your smile and see if you can tell which is the real smile and which is the passive smile.

p173.original: 批判性思维的应用：测谎仪真的能测出谎言吗
p173.en: Application of critical thinking: Can a lie detector really detect a lie?

p174.original: 测谎仪或“谎言探测”的测试基于这样的假设：当人们说谎时，会发出身体唤醒的信号。因此，大多数测谎仪会记录被测试者的心率、呼吸频率、排汗和血压。偶尔也会使用声纹分析。因此，该设备实际上是作为一个情绪唤醒探测器，而不能直接探测真相或谎言。它真的有效吗？让我们看看测谎仪是如何运作的。
p174.en: The test of a polygraph or “false detection” is based on the assumption that when people lie, they send a wake-up call. Therefore, most polygraphs record the heart rate, the frequency of breathing, sweating and blood pressure of the tested person. Voiceline analysis is used occasionally. The device is therefore in effect an emotional wake-up detector and cannot directly detect the truth or lies. Is it really working? Let's see how the polygraph works.

p175.original: 测谎者通常会使用行业内的一些技巧。他们可能会在面试开始时让被测试者相信这台机器是高度准确的。一个常见的策略是问一系列旨在激起明显情绪反应的问题。例如，“在你的生活中，你有没有拿过不属于自己的东西？”在另一种很受欢迎的方法中，测谎者使用欺骗性的刺激程序或“刺激测试”，在此过程中，被测试者从“堆叠”的卡片中抽一张卡片。然后，考官试图从被测试者的测谎反应中识别出这张卡片（APA，2004）。
p175.en: The polygrapher usually uses some of the techniques in the industry. They may convince the tested at the beginning of the interview that the machine is highly accurate. A common strategy is to ask a range of questions designed to provoke a clear emotional reaction. For example, “Have you ever taken anything that is not your own in your life? “In another popular way, the polygrapher uses a deceptive irritation procedure or “irritation test”, in which the tested person draws a card from a “clip” card. The examiner then attempted to identify the card from the test person's polygraph reaction (APA, 2004).

p176.original: 当真正的审问开始时，相关问题、无关问题和控制问题等会结合在一起。无关问题（“你现在正坐着吗？”）旨在引出真实的答案，同时辅以与说实话相一致的身体反应。控制性问题（“你对父母撒过谎吗？”）旨在引起一种焦虑的、情绪化的反应模式。然后，测谎者将被测试者对这两类问题的反应与对相关问题（“你偷了珠宝吗？”）的反应进行比较。一般认为，犯罪嫌疑人对这些问题的反应要比对无关和控制问题的反应更强烈[1]。
p176.en: When the real interrogation begins, the related issues, irrelevant issues and control issues are combined. Doesn't matter. The aim is to elicit real answers, accompanied by physical reactions consistent with the truth. Control problems. It is an emotional response model designed to provoke anxiety. Then, the polygrapher will have the tester's reaction to these two types of questions and the related questions: “Did you steal the jewellery? A comparison of reactions. The suspect's response to these issues is generally considered to be stronger [1] than his response to irrelevant and control issues.

p178.original: 如果你不熟悉有关“测谎仪”的争议，那么你就应该先了解双方的立场（这对任何问题都是不错的方法）。你可以在你最喜欢的互联网搜索引擎中输入“测谎仪”。我们已经做过这类工作，也搜索了科学文献，以下是我们发现的情况。
p178.en: If you are not familiar with the dispute about the polygraph, then you should first understand the positions of both parties (this is a good way of doing anything). You can enter a polygraph in your favorite Internet search engine. We've done this work, we've searched the scientific literature, and here's what we found.

p179.original: 假阳性和假标准的问题
p179.en: The problem of false positives and false criteria

p180.original: 毫无疑问，做坏事的人有时确实会在测谎仪面前供认不讳。但是，大多数人没有意识到，测谎仪也可以轻易地把无辜的人送进监狱，而让有罪的人逍遥法外（Aftergood，2000）。为了说明这一点，我们假设测谎仪的准确率为95%（这只是一种猜测，因为没有人真的知道它的准确率）。现在想象一下，你的公司安排500名员工参加测谎测试，以找出是谁偷了办公用品。再假设他们中只有4%（500人中有20人）有真正的偷窃行为（这并不是一个不合理的估计）。所以，如果测谎仪的准确率达到95%，它就能准确地识别出这20个小偷中的19个。但问题是如果测试的准确率达到95%，那么它也会给出5%的假阳性，错误地指证5%的无辜员工。在你的480名无辜员工中，测谎仪会错误地将24人列为说谎者；也就是说，最终被错误指控说谎的人可能比被正确指控说谎的人要多。这在一项对嫌疑犯的实际研究中得到了证实，这些嫌疑犯后来要么被定罪，要么被宣告无罪。测谎结果并不比抛硬币好多少（Brett et al.，1986）。
p180.en: There is no doubt that those who do bad things sometimes confess to themselves in front of the polygraph. However, the majority of the population is not aware that a polygraph can easily send innocent people to prison and those guilty go unpunished (Affergood, 2000). To illustrate this, we assume that the polygraph is 95% accurate (this is just a guess, because no one really knows its accuracy). Now imagine that your company has arranged for 500 employees to take a polygraph test to find out who stole office supplies. It is also assumed that only 4 per cent of them (20 out of 500) have genuine theft (not an unreasonable estimate). Thus, if the polygraph is up to 95 per cent, it will be able to identify 19 of the 20 thieves accurately. The problem, however, is that if the test reaches 95 per cent, it also gives a 5 per cent false positive, wrongly identifying 5 per cent of innocent employees. Of your 480 innocent employees, the polygraph wrongly lists 24 as liars; In other words, there may be more people who are ultimately wrongly accused of lying than those who are rightly accused of lying. This was confirmed in a practical study of suspects who were later either convicted or acquitted. The results of the polygraph are not much better than the drop of coins (Brett et al., 1986).

p181.original: 但这还并非唯一的问题。记住，接受测谎仪测试的人清楚地知道自己什么时候看起来是嫌疑人，所以，有些人会对关键问题做出更强烈的反应，即便他们是无辜的。相反，有些人会给出欺骗性的回答，因为他们压抑或歪曲了自己的情绪反应。为了做到这一点，他们可能会使用简单的身体运动、药物或生物反馈训练。在此过程中，人们学会控制某些生理反应，如排汗或心率（Saxe et al.，1985）。无论哪种方式，测谎者都有可能误将无辜的人认定为有罪，而无法发现说谎者。
p181.en: But this is not the only issue. Remember that people who are tested for a lie detector clearly know when they appear to be suspects, so some will react more strongly to the key issues, even if they are innocent. On the contrary, some give deceptive answers because they suppress or distort their emotional reactions. In order to do so, they may use simple physical exercise, medication or biological feedback training. In doing so, people learn to control certain physiological reactions, such as sweating or heart rate (Saxe et al., 1985). In either way, a liar detector may wrongly criminalize an innocent person and not find a liar.

p182.original: 关于测谎术的一个同样严重的问题是，无论是测谎还是解释测谎结果，都没有公认的标准。不同的检查人员会根据同一测谎仪记录的结果得出不同的结论。
p182.en: An equally serious problem with polygraphing is that there are no generally accepted criteria for both the polygraph and the interpretation of the results. Different inspectors draw different conclusions based on the results of the same polygraph records.

p183.original: 测谎仪的经济和政治利益
p183.en: The economic and political benefits of polygraphs

p184.original: 我们认为，由于涉及经济和政治利益，测谎仪可能会“一意孤行”。一个强大的测谎仪行业的经济利益在于，让公众相信测谎仪确实可以分辨出说真话的人和说谎的人。警察和刑事检察官也有政治利益，即拥有一个快速结案和定罪的“科学”方法。大多数支持测谎仪的“数据”实际上就是来自这些证据。
p184.en: We believe that, because of the economic and political interests involved, the polygraph may be “apologetic”. The economic interest of a strong lie detector industry lies in convincing the public that a lie detector can indeed distinguish between a person who tells the truth and a person who lies. The police and the criminal prosecutor also have a political interest in having a “scientific” method of expeditious resolution and conviction. Most of the “data” supporting the polygraph are in fact from these evidences.

p185.original: 那么，我们对测谎仪能得出什么结论？
p185.en: So, what can we say about the polygraph?

p186.original: 美国国会已禁止在工作选拔和政府的大多数领域使用测谎仪，除非是针对高风险职位。美国国家科学院（The National Academies of Sciences，2003）在一份报告中甚至说，测谎仪过于粗糙，无法用于甄别可能的恐怖分子或其他国家安全风险。本书的作者也赞同这一观点。
p186.en: The United States Congress has banned the use of polygraphs in job selection and most areas of government, except for high-risk positions. The National Academy of Sciences (the National Academy of Sciences, 2003) even stated in a report that the polygraph was too crude to be used to identify potential terrorists or other national security risks. The authors of this book share this view.

p187.original: 就刑事调查而言，我们发现美国各州在测谎仪证据的可行性方面存在一些拼凑补缀。很少有哪个州会彻底禁止使用测谎仪。有20个州规定，只有在双方同意的情况下才允许使用这种证据。然而，在少数几个州里，即使违背了辩方的意愿，测谎结果在法庭上仍然会被普遍参考（Gruben & Madsen，2005）。那么，在刑事案件中使用测谎仪的问题上，你的立场是什么？测谎仪有时会迫使嫌疑人招供，这一事实是否为它的使用提供了正当理由？
p187.en: In the case of criminal investigations, we have found some patchworks in the United States states on the feasibility of evidence for polygraphs. Very few states will completely ban the use of polygraphs. Twenty states allow the use of such evidence only with the consent of both parties. However, in a few states, even against the wishes of the defence, the results of the polygraph are still widely referred to in court (Gruben & Madsen, 2005). So what is your position on the use of polygraphs in criminal cases? Does the fact that a lie detector sometimes compels a suspect to confess, justify its use?

p189.original: 对测谎仪的管控促进了测谎的替代方法的发展（Capps & Ryan，2005；Lane，2006）。大部分的工作都是通过纸笔工具进行的，通常被称为“诚信测试”。这些仪器的效果如何？根据美国心理学会和美国政府技术评估办公室的报告，效果不是很好。和测谎仪一样，它们也有很高的假阳性率。
p189.en: The control of polygraphs has facilitated the development of alternative methods of polygraphing (Capps & Ryan, 2005); Lane, 2006. Most of the work is carried out through paper and pen tools, often referred to as “good faith tests”. How are these instruments working? According to reports from the American Psychological Association and the United States Government Technical Assessment Office, the results were not very good. Like polygraphs, they have a high degree of false positives.

p190.original: 保罗·埃克曼，也就是那个研究面部表情跨文化一致性的人，发现说谎者经常表现出短暂的“微表情”和其他非语言线索。在一项研究中，埃克曼和他的同事莫琳·奥沙利文（Maureen O'sullivan）发现，有些人特别擅长识别谎言，但这只是极少数人。在他们的测试中，大多数人的成绩和随机水平差不多。尽管如此，埃克曼和奥沙利文还是希望能学到那些最擅长检测谎言的人的诀窍，并将其传授给警察和其他关注犯罪和安全问题的人（Adelson，2004）。
p190.en: Paul Eckerman, the one who studied cross-cultural consistency in facial expression, found that liars often showed short “micro-expressions” and other non-verbal leads. In one study, Ekman and his colleague Maureen O'Sullivan found that some people were particularly good at identifying lies, but that was only a few. In their tests, most of them performed at a level similar to that of random. Despite this, Ekman and Osharivin hope to learn the know-how of those who are best at detecting lies and to pass it on to the police and others concerned with crime and security (Adelson, 2004).

p191.original: 此外，一些研究人员将关注点转向了大脑扫描技术，我们看看他们是否能识别说谎者（Ross，2003）。一种被称为P300的特定脑电波成分与各种注意力（如听到一个人的名字）线索有关，但研究表明，说谎也能诱发这种脑电波成分。此外，功能磁共振成像显示，说谎激活了与说真话有关的所有大脑区域，以及更多的区域。精神病学家丹尼尔·朗勒本（Daniel Langleben）认为，这表明，说谎并不是完全与说真话分开，而是说谎者必须在真话的基础上进行操作。所有这些都引起了人们的关注，即基于大脑扫描的测谎术有太多的炒作和太少的确凿证据（Gamer，2009；Langleben et al.，2002；Stix，2008）。此外，一些神经科学家担心，通过直接窥视人的大脑以“读”出他们个人思想的神经痕迹可能会存在伦理问题（Pearson，2006）。
p191.en: In addition, some researchers have turned their focus to brain scanning techniques, and we will see if they can identify the liars (Ross, 2003). A specific brain wave component known as P300 is associated with various lines of attention (e.g. hearing a person's name), but studies have shown that lying can also induce such brain waves. In addition, the MRI image shows that lying activates all the brain areas associated with telling the truth, and more. According to the psychiatrist Daniel Langleben, this suggests that lying is not entirely separate from telling the truth, but rather that the liar must operate on the basis of the truth. All of this has raised concerns that brain scan-based polygraphs have too many improvisations and too little conclusive evidence (Gamer, 2009); Langleben et al., 2002; Stix, 2008. In addition, some neuroscientists fear that there may be ethical problems in “reading” the neurological traces of their individual minds by looking directly at the human brain (Pearson, 2006).

p192.en: The potential advantage of these new brain scanning techniques is that they bypass the anxiety-reaction route used by the polygraph. By recording neuroactivity, it is closer to the real human mind. But what is the effect of these alternatives? At least not good enough for the courts and the police.
